Website.title: MenuGauge — Menu bar system monitor
Website.description: CPU, GPU, temperature, fan speed, memory, disk and network speed in the macOS menu bar. One native panel, updated every 2 seconds.
Website.requirements: macOS 13 or later · Apple Silicon and Intel
Website.previewAlt: MenuGauge overview: CPU usage, CPU temperature and GPU usage on top, then fan speed, available memory, available disk and network.
Website.settingsAlt: MenuGauge Settings, with a switch for each menu-bar reading, launch at login, and Quit MenuGauge.
Website.workflowTitle: Look up. Then get back to it.
Website.openBody: Click the menu bar icon. The overview lists every reading and refreshes every 2 seconds. Click the icon again, click outside, or press Esc to close.
Website.chooseBody: The Settings tab turns each menu-bar reading on or off. The overview still shows all of them, and your choice is saved.
Website.stayBody: One 2-second timer samples the system. MenuGauge stays in the background, with no Dock icon, and follows the system light or dark appearance. On a short screen, the panel scrolls.
Website.featureIntro: The overview puts CPU usage, CPU temperature and GPU usage on top, then fan speed, available memory, available disk and network.
Website.metricsBody: CPU and GPU usage, CPU temperature, and the average speed of every fan, rounded to a whole RPM. A stopped fan counts as 0 RPM. A Mac with no fans shows N/A. A missing fan reading is not filled in from the others. On Apple Silicon, temperature uses the SMC sensors Lemon uses for that M1–M5 chip, averaging only values above 20 °C and below 110 °C. A failed read is left out. M1 Pro, M1 Max, M1 Ultra, M2 and M3 include some GPU sensors; M4 and M5 do not. Intel uses the first valid CPU sensor. An unknown chip, or no valid reading, shows as unavailable. PMU and other HID readings are not used as the CPU temperature.
Website.capacityBody: Memory follows Activity Monitor: app memory, wired and compressed. Disk is the system volume, used and total, in decimal GB — the same units as Finder and System Settings. Network shows upload and download on physical en* interfaces. If a VPN or filter such as CorpLink keeps the inbound counter at zero, download shows -- instead of a misleading 0, and returns when inbound traffic is counted again.
Website.menuBody: Enabled readings use a compact two-line layout. When the menu bar runs out of room, values hide from the right and come back on their own. Turn every reading off and the fan icon remains. Launch at login is on the same tab.
Website.heatBody: From 75 °C, or from 80% memory or disk, the color moves from orange toward red. It reaches the top of that scale at 85 °C or 90%. Words stay with the color.
Website.controlsTitle: Open it, then put it away.
Website.faqInstallBody: Requires macOS 13 or later. It is a universal app for Apple Silicon and Intel. The current download is a notarized disk image: open it and drag MenuGauge.app into Applications. If a release is still a zip, unpack it and drag the app across the same way. A notarized Developer ID build opens normally. An older ad-hoc build is blocked by Gatekeeper the first time you open it after a browser or AirDrop download: right-click the app, choose Open, and confirm, or allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
Website.faqLogin: Why does launch at login need approval?
Website.faqLoginBody: The switch uses the system login item on macOS 13 and later. The first time you turn it on, allow MenuGauge in System Settings → General → Login Items. If approval is still required, the panel links to System Settings. If it fails, MenuGauge shows the reason and leaves the switch in its real state.
Website.faqLanguages: Is it available in my language?
Website.faqLanguagesBody: MenuGauge follows your macOS language. It includes English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Hindi, Spanish, French, Bengali, Russian and Portuguese. Any other language uses English. This website has the same 11 languages; choose yours in the menu above.
Website.closingTitle: Keep an eye on it from the menu bar.
Website.footer: A native macOS menu bar monitor. No third-party dependencies.
